title: Iran war: US to spend $58.6 billion in missile deal with Lockheed Martin amid depleting critical Patriot interceptors
content:
• The US Army awarded Lockheed Martin a contract worth up to $58.6 billion to manufacture Patriot interceptor missiles.
• This Lockheed Martin contract converts a previous one-year deal of $4.7 billion into a seven-year draft agreement for procurement from fiscal years 2026 through 2032.
• Lockheed Martin plans to invest between $8 billion and $9 billion through 2030 to upgrade facilities and aims to triple PAC-3 MSE interceptor missile production capacity by the end of 2030.

title: US launches fresh strikes on Iranian military targets after missile attack on American forces in Jordan
content:
• Brent crude prices surged over 7% on Wednesday, climbing above $88 a barrel, due to renewed hostilities and concerns over supplies from the Strait of Hormuz.
• US and Saudi Arabia launched joint strikes against Iran-backed armed groups in Iraq, resulting in at least 20 members of Iraq's Popular Mobilisation Forces (PMF) killed and 32 wounded.
• The United States launched fresh strikes on Iranian military targets early Thursday, a day after Iran confirmed firing ballistic missiles at US forces in Jordan and targeting ships in the Strait of Hormuz.

title: Iran war: Why US military may ban cell phones for some troops in Middle East? Report says Tehran ‘benefiting’ from...
content:
• Admiral Brad Cooper, head of US Central Command, warned in a July 28 letter that Iran is benefiting from online posts and cellphone videos shared by troops, which aid in assessing the success or failure of its strikes.
• The conflict with Iran has led to 18 US troops dead and over 600 wounded since Feb. 28, deepening concerns among Americans.
• Due to operational security concerns, some US troops in Jordan have been informed that their phones will be confiscated in the coming days, following incidents like an Iranian attack on the Muwaffaq Salti Air Base on July 17.

title: Delhi-Hyderabad IndiGo flight carrying Revanth Reddy lands safely after rain-triggered go-around: Report
content:
• IndiGo has appointed Kiran Thadimarri as its new Chief Financial Officer (CFO) with effect from July 28, succeeding Gaurav Negi.
• IndiGo reported its second consecutive quarterly loss and projected largely flat capacity growth for the current quarter.
• IndiGo's operating margins faced pressure due to a sharp increase in jet fuel prices after the Iran conflict drove global crude oil prices above $100 a barrel.

title: Minister Goyal says India-US trade deal can move ahead once tariff edge is secured
content:
• Under the US Section 301 process, India was placed in the lower 10% tariff band, while competing exporters like China and Vietnam were assigned a higher 12.5% rate, providing Indian exporters a relative tariff advantage in the US market.
• The UK Free Trade Agreement came into effect on 15 July, providing Indian exports zero-duty access to the UK market.
• The India-European Union Free Trade Agreement is expected to come into force in the first quarter of 2027, opening access to a market of 27 countries with a combined GDP of nearly $20 trillion.

title: ‘This crosses a line’: FIFA faces backlash over selling World Cup stake, Donald Trump connection
content:
• On 28 July, FIFA announced plans to create a $20 billion (₹1.91 lakh crore) subsidiary for its commercial and event operations, with external investors allowed to buy up to 20%.
• FIFA aims to raise up to $4.2 billion (₹40,215 crore) from selling a stake in its new subsidiary, reportedly to fund football development programmes worldwide.
• The FIFA World Cup 2026 introduced hydration breaks, dividing each half for the first time, a change predicted by Diego Maradona in 2018 and estimated to be worth 'a billion dollars'.

title: Comparative advantage for India key to US pact: Piyush Goyal
content:
• The first tranche of the bilateral trade agreement between India and the US was announced on February 3rd.
• Indian exports have grown 15% so far in the current fiscal year (April-July), despite ongoing global disruptions.
• India's current $4 trillion economy is on track to become a $30 trillion economy by 2047.

title: Services index shows 16 sub-sectors recorded double-digit growth in May
content:
• The Banking sector recorded a 12.1% growth in May 2026, as per the trial Index of Services Production (ISP) released by the Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation (MoSPI).
• The Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation (MoSPI) released the trial Index of Services Production (ISP) for May 2026, using 2024-25 as its base year.
• Indices for the Railways, Banking, and Insurance sub-sectors within the Index of Services Production are based on provisional monthly data and will undergo revision on an annual basis.

title: Up to 12 pc of non-agri jobs at risk of substitution due to Gen AI: Report
content:
• Wall Street brokerage Goldman Sachs estimates that 8-12% of India's non-agricultural employment is at risk of substitution due to generative AI.
• The Goldman Sachs report views generative AI as a medium-term positive for India's overall growth outlook.
• Gen-AI adoption is projected to lift India's annual labour-productivity growth by approximately 0.4 percentage points over a 10-year period.

title: Indian economy shows recovery despite global uncertainties, private investment gains momentum: Report
content:
• According to a report by Kotak Institutional Equities, industrial credit in India expanded 18 per cent year-on-year in May 2026.
• The Kotak Institutional Equities report identifies the sharp increase in credit flowing to industries as a strong indicator of India's economic recovery and a broad-based pick-up in private sector investment.
• India's macroeconomic outlook has become uncertain due to the re-escalation of the Iran-US conflict, leading to higher crude oil prices, and deficient rainfall during the monsoon season, raising concerns over food inflation.
